newsitem.title: LEBANON: New appeal against Lebanon election results.
newsitem.headline: New appeal against Lebanon election results.

text.p: An opposition candidate defeated in Lebanon's parliamentary polls has appealed against election results, alleging that Syria issued a ban on his re-election at the request of President Elias Hrawi.
Mikhael al-Daher, a Christian deputy defeated in north Lebanon, petitioned Lebanon's constitutional court before Saturday's deadline for appeals against the August 28 election results.

Another nine losers -- four Christians and six Moslems -- have filed similar appeals, alleging vote-rigging and abuse by pro-government candidates who crushed the opposition in all five rounds of voting. They asked the court to reject the results and declare them winners.

Daher said the "information and security service" -- a codeword for Syria's intelligence service in Lebanons -- pressured hundreds of key local electoral figures in Akkar district to support his rival Fawzi Hobeish. He said the pressure was imposed at Hrawi's request.
Daher was one of a handful of deputies who opposed a constitutional amendment last year extending Hrawi's term by three years.

Daher cited in his appeal "flagrant interventions on the part of Lebanese civil and security officials" and said methods used against him and his supporters ranged between "verbal threats and detention of dozens for hours in cells under inhumane conditions".
The 10-member constituional court, formed last year, gives first-time losing candidates the chance to appeal against the results. The court's decisions are final.
